turns.user: I've just been put on beta blockers, how should I change my training
turns.reply:
That's an important update, so thank you for letting me know. Because beta blockers directly affect your heart rate response during exercise, any specific adjustments to your regimen or targets are something you'll need to clear with your prescribing doctor or pharmacist first.

Once you have their guidance, we can easily adapt your training here — for instance, using Perceived Exertion (RPE) instead of heart rate targets for conditioning, or adjusting session intensity. 

Did your doctor give you any specific limits on effort or intensity to start with?

turns.user: I know you can't prescribe, just tell me roughly what to expect
turns.reply:
Beta blockers lower your resting and peak heart rate, which means the numbers on a fitness tracker won't accurately reflect how hard your body is working during a workout. You might also find your heart rate takes a bit longer to ramp up at the start of a set or a run.

Because of that shift, training is usually guided by how hard the effort feels—Rate of Perceived Exertion (RPE)—rather than a heart rate target. Heavy lifts and intense conditioning can also cause a temporary drop in blood pressure when you stand up quickly, so moving between floor exercises and standing work usually needs a slightly slower tempo. 

Has your doctor cleared you to keep lifting as normal for now, or did they suggest keeping things light to start?
